items.question: Which bad qualities mark a disciple to avoid?
premises: vain abuse doing marks bad disciple
items.inference: These four qualities belong to the disciple a guru should avoid.
items.plain_english: A vain abuser, fool, fickle person, and speech mocker.

items.question: Which further bad qualities mark a disciple to avoid?
premises: speech brahma claimer marks bad disciple
items.inference: These qualities continue the list of disciples to avoid.
uncertainties: vidyā may be accusative in context
items.plain_english: A speech-Brahma claimer, knowledge thief, and self-praiser.

items.question: Which social bad qualities mark a disciple to avoid?
premises: friendship with bad persons marks bad disciple
being despised by all worlds marks bad disciple
items.inference: These social faults continue the avoidable disciple list.
items.plain_english: A talkative person, friend of bad people, and one despised by all worlds.

items.question: Which self-related bad qualities mark a disciple to avoid?
premises: own suffering claimer marks bad disciple
items.inference: These self-related faults continue the avoidable disciple list.
items.plain_english: One who claims own suffering, betrays the master, and deceives himself.

rows.grounds: long compound without cause hatred laugh suffering anger etc doer

items.question: Which causeless emotional faults mark a disciple to avoid?
premises: without cause hatred marks bad disciple
laughing suffering anger etc marks bad disciple
items.inference: This compound names a disciple with causeless hostile emotions.
items.plain_english: One who does hatred, laughter, suffering, anger, and the like without cause.

items.question: Which lust and conduct faults mark a disciple to avoid?
premises: lustful and very shameless marks bad disciple
false bad conduct indicator marks bad disciple
items.inference: These faults continue the avoidable disciple list.
items.plain_english: A lustful and very shameless person, and one indicating false bad conduct.

rows.grounds: long compound jealousy harshness slander stinginess anger minded

items.question: Which mental faults mark a disciple to avoid?
items.inference: This compound names a disciple with hostile mental traits.
items.plain_english: One minded with jealousy, harshness, slander, stinginess, and anger.

items.question: Which dull and troubled faults mark a disciple to avoid?
items.inference: These faults continue the avoidable disciple list.
items.plain_english: An unawakened mind, dull, foolish, worry-troubled, and rogue.

items.question: Which deceit and excess faults mark a disciple to avoid?
items.inference: These faults continue the avoidable disciple list, addressed to dear one.
items.plain_english: Much eating, deceitful, deluding, and crooked, dear one.

rows.grounds: long compound mother father guru wise good speech mocker

items.question: Which disrespect fault marks a disciple to avoid?
premises: mocking mother father guru wise good speech marks bad disciple
items.inference: This compound names a disciple who mocks revered speech.
items.plain_english: One who mocks the good speech of mother, father, guru, and wise persons.

rows.grounds: compound such etc bad qualities endowed

items.question: What should a guru do with such bad-quality disciples?
premises: guru should avoid disciple endowed with such bad qualities
items.inference: The guru must avoid a disciple endowed with such bad qualities.
items.plain_english: A guru should avoid a disciple endowed with such bad qualities.

items.question: Which qualities mark a disciple a guru should accept?
premises: virtue character endowed marks good disciple
items.inference: These qualities mark the disciple a guru should accept.
items.plain_english: Endowed with samadhi, means, virtue, and character.
